response: Although elevated leukocyte count and CRP value cannot effectively establish the diagnosis of acute appendicitis in the elderly, unelevated values can help exclude it. In other words, if an elderly patient has unelevated leukocyte count and CRP value, despite clinical symptoms and signs indicating acute appendicitis, appendectomy is not recommended. This suggests that leukocyte and CRP measurements can be useful in ruling out acute appendicitis in the elderly, but should be considered in conjunction with clinical assessment.
